## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Water Movement

GRACE Follow-On uses two satellites, flying one behind the other about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart, to investigate changes in how mass is distributed on Earth.

As the pair passes a larger mass concentration, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther ahead of the trailing satellite. The satellites’ changing separation is measured and used to infer shifts in mass; it is not a direct measurement or image of groundwater.

Those inferred shifts help scientists investigate changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
